Facet reliability and separation snapshot bar plot

Source: R/api-plotting-secondary.R
plot_reliability_snapshot.Rd

Compact facet-level visual of the Wright & Masters (1982) separation, strata, and reliability indices that diagnose_mfrm() computes. Helpful as a single small figure for "are persons / raters / criteria distinguishable?" review. These are Rasch/FACETS-style separation indices on the fitted logit scale, not ICCs; use compute_facet_icc() for the complementary observed-score variance-share view.

Usage

plot_reliability_snapshot(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  metric = c("reliability", "separation", "strata"),
  preset = c("standard", "publication", "compact", "monochrome"),
  draw = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

An mfrm_fit from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional diagnose_mfrm() output. Computed on demand when omitted.

metric

"reliability" (default), "separation", or "strata".

preset

Visual preset.

draw

If TRUE, draw with base graphics.

Value

An mfrm_plot_data whose data slot bundles a tidy Facet, Metric, Value data frame. When present in the supplied diagnostics, precision tier, reliability use/basis, formal-inference flag and model-summary notes are retained alongside each plotted value.

Details

High Person separation reliability indicates distinguishable abilities. High rater separation reliability indicates distinguishable severities, not agreement between raters. If raters should be interchangeable, reliable severity differences merit review. Low rater separation reliability can also reflect imprecise estimates and does not establish agreement. The index does not test every rater pair or measure the practical size of severity differences. Examine estimated severities and their uncertainty, and use interrater_agreement_table() for observed agreement.

The separation-reliability formula is shared across facets, but the facet's role changes its interpretation. Person separation reliability is analogous to test reliability, not numerically identical to Cronbach's alpha; MML Person rows using EAP/posterior SD also have the limitations described in mfrmr-package. No universal adequate/strong reference lines are drawn. Reliability, separation and Strata use approximate marginal-SE variance subtraction and do not propagate covariance among estimates, even when the SEs come from joint information. Model and fit-adjusted indices are not confidence limits; Strata does not identify actual groups. Ordinary JML uses exploratory location precision; these indices are screening summaries, not structural confidence intervals. Corrected-JML RootSE is not an input to these indices. Corrected JML and two-family GPCM are unavailable here, including when diagnostics are supplied. The returned plot retains interpretation notes for saved reuse.

Migration in 0.2.4

This renderer is internal. Use the corresponding plot() route in mfrmr_plot_migration; the former exported name is no longer available.

Session plot defaults

Set options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "publication") to choose a session default for plotting functions that expose the common preset argument. The supported values are "standard", "publication", "compact" and "monochrome". Precedence is an explicit call argument, then the session option, then "standard". For example, preset = "standard" overrides a session set to "monochrome". Explicit preset = NULL retains the earlier package-default behavior; it does not read the session option. Invalid session values cause an error only when that option is needed.

The category-curve, data-quality, fit-review, connectivity and network routes of plot() for report bundles use the same option through .... Plots without a common preset argument, including extended-model plots with their own palette controls, keep their own settings. This option selects a preset, not a universal theme or a guarantee that all renderers implement every appearance control identically.

New plot payloads retain the resolved preset for supported saved-data rendering. Converting an existing payload with as_ggplot() uses its saved appearance, even after the session option changes. A call that creates a new plot from a fit or statistical result uses the current default. For a reproducible script, supply preset explicitly or set the option in that script. Saving only the fitted model does not save a session option. No global ggplot theme is changed.

Restore previous settings with old <- options(mfrmr.plot_preset = "monochrome") followed by options(old). Use options(mfrmr.plot_preset = NULL) to remove the option. The preset changes appearance, not estimates, confidence levels or diagnostic thresholds.

References

Linacre, J. M. Facets documentation, Reliability - separation - strata. https://www.winsteps.com/facetman/reliability.htm

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
p <- plot(fit, type = "reliability", draw = FALSE)
p$data$table
#>       Facet      Metric     Value PrecisionTier ReliabilityUse
#> 1     Rater reliability 0.9031009   exploratory screening_only
#> 2    Person reliability 0.9005676   exploratory screening_only
#> 3 Criterion reliability 0.8852451   exploratory screening_only
#>                                                          ReliabilityBasis
#> 1 Approximate marginal-SE variance subtraction; covariance not propagated
#> 2 Approximate marginal-SE variance subtraction; covariance not propagated
#> 3 Approximate marginal-SE variance subtraction; covariance not propagated
#>   SupportsFormalInference
#> 1                   FALSE
#> 2                   FALSE
#> 3                   FALSE
#>                                               ModelSummaryNote
#> 1   Computed over 4 of 4 levels with finite estimates and SEs.
#> 2 Computed over 48 of 48 levels with finite estimates and SEs.
#> 3   Computed over 4 of 4 levels with finite estimates and SEs.
# High Person value: distinguishable abilities.
# High rater value: distinguishable severities, not agreement.
# Low rater value: not proof of agreement; inspect estimation precision.
p$data$notes
#>             Type
#> 1 interpretation
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Text
#> 1 Separation reliability describes differences among facet locations relative to their estimation errors. High Person values indicate distinguishable abilities; high rater values indicate distinguishable severities, not inter-rater agreement. Low rater values can also reflect imprecision and do not establish agreement. The index does not test every rater pair or quantify the practical size of severity differences. Reliability, separation and Strata are approximate compatibility indices using marginal SEs; joint-information SEs do not validate this variance decomposition. They do not account for covariance among estimates. EAP-based separation is not posterior-variance EAP reliability. Model and fit-adjusted values are companion indices, not confidence limits. Strata describes hypothetical distinguishable strata, not discovered groups. Facet heterogeneity chi-square summaries use diagonal SE weights, not full-covariance joint tests. Ordinary JML uses exploratory location precision; these indices are screening summaries, not structural confidence intervals.
